hot.pointer_line: On now: the trawlers back since 1 October, palamida on the slab and lakerda curing, a sea still warm enough to swim, pomegranates and quinces at the laiki, clocks back on 25 October, Ohi Day on 28 October, the Authentic Marathon on 8 November and the Polytechnio march on 17 November.

items.name: The trawlers are back
items.teaser: Four months of summer trawl closure ended on 1 October, and the Varvakios fish hall is deep again
items.story: From 1 June to 30 September the Greek bottom trawlers stay tied up, and summer fish comes off the small caiques: sardines, gavros, marides. On 1 October the closure lifts and the Varvakios fish hall changes within a week. Hake, sole, shrimp and koutsomoures, the small red mullet, are back on the ice beside the last of the palamida. Walk the hall between 05:30 and 08:30, when the slabs are fullest and the sellers shout loudest, and look for wet, bright fish with red gills rather than the uniform rows of farmed bream.
items.why: October and November give the widest choice of wild fish in the Athens year: this is the season to provision or to order whole fish.
facts: Trawl season reopened 1 Oct 2026; closed again 1 Jun-30 Sep 2027
Free to walk; fish by the kilo, prices change daily
Go 05:30-08:30, closed shoes for the wet floor

sources.label: Hellenic Coast Guard fisheries legislation: Royal Decree 917/1966 (trawl rules)

items.name: Palamida, and lakerda in the making
items.teaser: The bonito run that began in September is at its height, and the good ouzeris are salting it down
items.story: Palamida, Atlantic bonito, runs through the Aegean from September, and by October it is the fish of the moment on the counters: dark-fleshed, oily, best grilled the day it is bought. The part Athens prizes most comes later. Fillets are salted, then rested in brine and oil to become lakerda, the cured bonito the Constantinopolitan refugees brought to the city's ouzeris. The lakerda made from this autumn's fish reaches the tables in November and through the winter, sliced thick with red onion and a pour of oil beside a glass of ouzo.
items.why: Eat palamida grilled now and ask your ouzeri, from November, whether the lakerda is its own cure.
facts: Palamida Sep-Nov; house lakerda on the table from about November
Varvakios fish hall for the fish; ouzeris for the lakerda
A house cure is firm and pink-red; tinned or bought-in lakerda is soft and pale

items.name: The sea is still warm
items.teaser: The Saronic water stays swimmable through October and cools fast at the month's end
items.story: Travel climate guides put the average sea temperature off Athens at about 22 to 23 C in October, warmer than in June, because the sea holds the summer's heat long after the air has cooled. The beaches of the Athens Riviera, from Glyfada to Vouliagmeni, empty after the summer crowd, and on a still, sunny October morning the water is clear and calm. The same guides warn that the sea cools quickly in the last days of the month, so a mid-October swim is a safer promise than one in November.
items.why: Book the swim for the first half of the stay; by November only the hardy go in.
facts: Through October; cooler after about the 25th
Athens Riviera beaches, Glyfada to Vouliagmeni
Average figures, not a reading: check a marine forecast the day before

sources.label: Dave's Travel Pages: Greece weather in October (sea around 22-23C)

items.name: The October light, and the clocks go back
items.teaser: The low, honeyed light of October, and an hour back on Sunday 25 October
items.story: Athens in October is known for its low, warm light: the sun sits lower over the Saronic, the summer haze has gone, and the marble of the Acropolis and the Pentelic stone of the city turn gold in the late afternoon. On Sunday 25 October 2026 Greece leaves summer time: at 04:00 the clocks go back to 03:00. After that the evenings close an hour earlier by the clock, so a sunset walk on Filopappou or Lycabettus moves into the late afternoon.
items.why: After 25 October plan the hill walks an hour earlier than you would in summer.
facts: Phones change by themselves; ship's clocks and crew rotas do not

items.name: Orionids and Leonids
items.teaser: Two showers peak this autumn, both partly washed out by the Moon
items.story: The Orionids, debris from Halley's Comet, peak on the night of 21 to 22 October 2026, best in the hours before dawn on the 22nd. The Leonids follow on the night of 17 to 18 November. The American Meteor Society and the Almanac agree on both dates and both warn of the Moon: a waxing gibbous in October will hide all but the brightest meteors, and a Moon about half lit in November will interfere less. From the city only the brightest will show; from a dark Attica shore or a boat at anchor off the coast, the sky is better.
items.why: For the Orionids look after moonset, in the small hours of 22 October,, away from the city glow.
facts: Orionids night of 21-22 Oct 2026; Leonids night of 17-18 Nov 2026
Any dark spot away from Athens' lights
Expect only around 20 an hour at best for the Orionids under a dark sky, fewer with the Moon up

items.name: Pomegranates, quinces and the first horta
items.teaser: The neighbourhood markets turn red and yellow, and the first rains bring the wild greens
items.story: October at the Athens laiki, the weekly street market, is pomegranates split to show their seeds, hard yellow quinces sold for baking with meat or boiling into spoon sweets, and new-crop nuts. After the first autumn rains the women from the villages bring wild horta, bitter greens to boil and dress with oil and lemon. The guide's month table also notes mushrooms coming down from Parnitha, but that is foragers' lore, not a market fact. The grapes of the September harvest are gone; this is the market of the cool months.
items.why: Buy quinces for the galley: baked with pork or beef they are the Athenian autumn in one dish.
facts: Any neighbourhood laiki; Varvakios fruit and vegetable side across Athinas
Horta depends on the rain: ask what was picked this week

items.name: The olive harvest and agourelaio
items.teaser: From November Attica picks its olives, and the first green, peppery oil reaches the shops
items.story: The olive harvest runs across Attica in November and December. The first oil to come off the presses, from olives picked still green, is agourelaio: cloudy, unfiltered, bright green, and peppery enough to catch the throat. It is a small, short-lived run, sold in the weeks after pressing by delis and by producers themselves, and it is at its best poured raw over boiled horta or grilled bread. Later in the winter the ordinary new-season oil, golder and softer, takes over.
items.why: If you are in Athens late in November, ask a deli for agourelaio and use it raw only.
facts: Harvest Nov-Dec; agourelaio from late November
Delis and producers around Athens and the Mesogaia
Unfiltered oil does not keep: buy small bottles and finish them within a few months

items.name: Epirus, at the night's end
items.teaser: The old guide says Epirus feeds the market round the clock on Fridays and Saturdays, October to Easter
items.story: Oinomageireio Epirus, inside the Varvakios meat market since 1898, is where Athens goes for patsas, the tripe soup, and magiritsa on any day of the year. The guide's market text says that from October to Easter it feeds the butchers around the clock on Fridays and Saturdays. Since Vasilis Akrivos took over in 2023, though, the kitchen is reported to keep market hours, about 07:00 to 18:00. So the dawn bowl, with the butchers in their aprons and vinegar-garlic at the table, is sure; the 3 a.m. one is not. Ring before you plan a night around it.
items.why: Come at 07:00 on a cold autumn morning for a white patsas sharpened with skordostoumpi.
facts: Daily from about 07:00 to 18:00 (all-night Fri-Sat, Oct-Easter, unconfirmed)

items.name: Ohi Day and the Polytechnio
items.teaser: Student parades on Wednesday 28 October, the march to the US embassy on Tuesday 17 November
items.story: On 28 October Greece marks the day in 1940 when Metaxas refused Mussolini's ultimatum: the Ohi, the No. In Athens the morning belongs to the schools, whose flag-bearers parade past the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Syntagma; in 2025 the student parade started at 11:00 and the centre's roads closed around it. On 17 November the city remembers the 1973 Polytechnic uprising against the junta: wreaths at the Polytechnic on Patission all day, then a long afternoon march to the US embassy. Both are public occasions; the Polytechnio march is political and heavily policed.
items.why: Avoid driving the centre on both mornings, and keep away from Exarchia the night of 17 November.
facts: Wed 28 Oct 2026 (public holiday); Tue 17 Nov 2026 (schools and universities closed)
Syntagma for 28 Oct; Polytechnic, Patission 42, to the US embassy for 17 Nov
The 2026 parade times and road closures are announced the week before

items.name: The Authentic Marathon, Sunday 8 November
items.teaser: The original course, Marathon to the Panathenaic Stadium, on the weekend of 7-8 November
items.story: The Athens Marathon, The Authentic, runs the 42.195 km from the town of Marathon to the marble Panathenaic Stadium, the route of the 1896 Olympic race and of the legend of the messenger. The 2026 race is on Sunday 8 November, with the shorter races of the same weekend on Saturday 7 November. Entries opened on 24 April 2026, and charity places are reported sold out. Spectators line Vasilissis Sofias and the last stretch to the stadium, and much of the east of the city closes to traffic for the morning.
items.why: Watch the last kilometre on Vasilissis Sofias or from the stadium, and expect no taxis across the centre until early afternoon.
facts: Sun 8 Nov 2026, start about 08:30 at Marathon; shorter races Sat 7 Nov
Marathon to the Panathenaic Stadium, Athens
Marathonos Avenue and the east of the centre close for the morning: move cars and deliveries to the day before

items.name: Barbara Kruger at the SNFCC, until 1 November
items.teaser: Thirteen outdoor works across the Niarchos park, her first statements in Greek, close on 1 November
items.story: Barbara Kruger's first solo show in Greece, Untitled (Pride and Contempt), has run since 28 April across the open spaces of the Stavros Niarchos Foundation Cultural Center. Thirteen new site-specific works sit on the canal, the esplanade and the buildings, the largest a 90-metre text on the National Library. For the first time her slogans are set in Greek, in her red and white. It is outdoors and free, and it ends on Sunday 1 November 2026.
items.why: Walk it at the end of the afternoon, then climb to the lighthouse terrace as the light goes.
facts: SNFCC, Syngrou 364, Kallithea: canal, esplanade and the National Library
Pair it with dinner at Delta on the opera roof, if you have booked

items.name: Tsiknopempti and Clean Monday, 2027
items.teaser: The whole city grills on Thursday 4 March 2027; Lent opens on Monday 15 March
items.story: The Orthodox calendar counts back from Easter. With Easter on 2 May 2027, Clean Monday, Kathara Deftera, the first day of Lent, falls on Monday 15 March, a public holiday, and Tsiknopempti, Smoky Thursday, falls eleven days before, on Thursday 4 March. On Tsiknopempti every grill in Athens is lit and the tavernas are full by evening. On Clean Monday the meat stops: lagana flatbread, taramosalata, octopus, halva, and kites flown from Filopappou hill. In 2026 the two days fell on 12 and 23 February.
items.why: Book the Tsiknopempti table days ahead; it is the busiest grill night of the year.
facts: Tsiknopempti Thu 4 Mar 2027; Clean Monday Mon 15 Mar 2027
Citywide; kites on Filopappou on Clean Monday
Buy lagana from a bakery the Sunday before: by Monday noon it is gone

items.name: Orthodox Easter, 2 May 2027
items.teaser: Good Friday 30 April, the midnight Resurrection, then spit-roast lamb on Sunday 2 May
items.story: Orthodox Easter 2027 falls on Sunday 2 May, five weeks after the Western Easter of 28 March. On Good Friday, 30 April, each parish carries its flower-covered epitaphios through the streets after dark. Near midnight on Saturday the lights go out in every church, the priest brings out the flame, and at 'Christos anesti' fireworks go off across the city; families then go home for magiritsa, the offal soup that ends the fast. Sunday is lamb on the spit. Easter Monday, 3 May, is a holiday too, and Athens half empties from Friday to Monday.
items.why: Book the post-midnight Saturday table well ahead; that is when the city eats.
facts: Good Friday 30 Apr; Easter Sunday 2 May; Easter Monday 3 May 2027
Every parish church; the city empties towards the villages
Many shops and suppliers close Friday to Monday: provision by Thursday

items.name: Dekapentavgoustos, 15 August
items.teaser: The Dormition holiday empties Athens, and many family tavernas close for one to three weeks
items.story: 15 August, the Dormition of the Virgin, is the high point of the Greek summer and a public holiday. Athenians leave for their islands and villages, and the city is quieter than at any other time of year. Many family tavernas, bakeries and small shops close for one to three weeks around it, while the serious restaurants increasingly stay open. The laikes run thin as producers take their own holiday, and the meltemi can keep the caiques in port. In 2027 the 15th is a Sunday.
items.why: Check every opening hour for the second half of August: it is the month this guide's data goes stale fastest.
facts: Sun 15 Aug 2027; closures roughly the first three weeks of August
Ring a venue the week before; a website's hours will not say it has shut

items.name: 25 March, Independence Day
items.teaser: The military parade passes Syntagma, the centre closes, and lunch is fried salt cod with skordalia
items.story: 25 March marks both the start of the 1821 War of Independence and the Annunciation. In Athens the armed forces parade past the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier and along Vasilissis Amalias and Panepistimiou, with the school parade the day before, and the centre is closed to traffic for the morning. The day is a fast-day exception within Lent: fish is allowed, so the city eats bakaliaros skordalia, fried salt cod with garlic purée. In 2027 it falls on a Thursday.
items.why: Book a bakaliaros lunch for after the parade; it is the dish of the day.
facts: Roads close early in the morning; walk in

items.name: 28 October, Ohi Day
items.teaser: The day Greece refused the 1940 ultimatum: flags, school parades and a public holiday
items.story: On 28 October 1940 the Greek prime minister Ioannis Metaxas answered Mussolini's ultimatum with a refusal, remembered in one word, Ohi, No. The day is a public holiday. In Athens it belongs to the schools: representative groups of pupils, scouts and guides parade past the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier at Syntagma, and every balcony flies a flag. The main military parade is held in Thessaloniki.
items.why: A good day to walk the centre, but drive around it.
facts: In 2025 the Athens student parade began at 11:00

items.name: 17 November, Polytechnio
items.teaser: Wreaths at the Polytechnic and a march to the US embassy for the 1973 uprising
items.story: On the night of 17 November 1973 a tank broke through the gate of the Athens Polytechnic on Patission and ended the student occupation against the colonels' junta. Every year the gate and the old buildings are covered in flowers for three days, and on the 17th a march leaves the Polytechnic in the afternoon for the US embassy on Vasilissis Sofias. Schools and universities close. The day is political and heavily policed, and the evening in Exarchia can turn to clashes.
items.why: Lay a carnation at the Polytechnic gate in the morning; leave the area before dark.
facts: Polytechnic, Patission 42, to the US embassy
Expect central roads along the route closed from mid-afternoon

items.name: The Athens Epidaurus Festival
items.teaser: Ancient drama at Epidaurus and new work in Athens, from June to the end of August
items.story: The Athens Epidaurus Festival is the Greek summer's main stage. Its 2026 edition, the 71st, ran from 1 June to 29 August, with the Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus from 20 June. In Athens the festival lives at Peiraios 260 while the Odeon of Herodes Atticus is closed for restoration. Epidaurus is about two hours by road from Athens; the performances begin after dark in a fourth-century BC theatre whose acoustics still carry a whisper to the top row. The 2027 programme and dates have not yet been announced.
items.why: One night at Epidaurus is worth the drive: arrive early and take a cushion.
facts: June to late August; 2026 ran 1 Jun-29 Aug; 2027 dates not yet announced
Ancient Theatre of Epidaurus; Peiraios 260, Athens
Coaches run from Athens on performance nights; book with the ticket

items.name: Markopoulo's Festival Trygou
items.teaser: Savatiano country treads its grapes at the old railway station, usually at harvest time in early September
items.story: Markopoulo, in the Mesogaia 40 minutes east of the centre, is the heart of Attica's savatiano and retsina country. Each year at the grape harvest the municipality holds its Festival Trygou at the old railway station: grape treading and wine-making shown the old way, local wine and food, concerts, folk dance and theatre. Visit Greece describes it only as late summer, timed to the harvest; the guide places it in the first week of September. The 2026 dates were not found, and 2027 has not been announced.
items.why: Combine it with a winery visit in the Mesogaia while the presses are working.
facts: Usually early September; 2027 dates not yet announced
Check the Municipality of Markopoulo's announcements in August

sources.label: Visit Greece: Harvest Festival of the Municipality of Markopoulo

items.name: The summer trawl ban
items.teaser: Trawlers stop from 1 June to 30 September, and summer fish comes from the small boats
items.story: Greek bottom trawlers are tied up from 1 June to 30 September to let the stocks breed. Through the summer the fish counters carry what the small caiques bring in with nets and lines: sardines, gavros, marides, red mullet, the occasional sea bream, and in July and August the meltemi can keep even those in port. Hake, sole and shrimp return when the trawlers sail again on 1 October. In summer, ask whether a fish is wild and from which boat; an unusually full counter in August is often yesterday's catch or farmed.
items.why: In summer order the small fish; save the hake and the shrimp for October.
facts: Wild fish is labelled with its catch method and area by law: read the ticket
